judged_text: The controller enqueues a retrieve_topic Sidekiq job for every request that misses the topic lookup, with no rate limit at the enqueue site; the 60-second throttle lives inside TopicRetriever.retrieved_recently? keyed per-URL, so distinct URL paths each get a fresh throttle budget and the enqueue itself is unthrottled and unauthenticated. An unauthenticated client spamming /embed/best?embed_url=http://<embeddable_host>/<random> floods the Sidekiq queue with jobs (each job performs a Redis SETNX plus potentially an outbound HTTP fetch), exhausting background-job capacity; the per-URL Redis key provides no defense because the attacker varies the path.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil, it unconditionally enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` (no auth check, no rate limiting at enqueue time). The only throttling shown is inside `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?`, keyed as `retrieved:#{@embed_url}` (full URL string), so varying the URL path (`http://<embeddable_host>/<random>`) yields distinct Redis keys and bypasses the 60s throttle. Since `ensure_embeddable` only validates `request.referer` host equals `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` (a header clients can supply) and does not require a logged-in user, an attacker can flood Sidekiq with jobs that will at least do Redis work and may trigger outbound fetches via `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (`open(url)`), exhausting background capacity.
